name: Role-based access control
description: The system must support distinct roles for pharmacists, technicians, cashiers, branch managers, and administrators, with role-specific permissions and an audit trail for medication-related actions.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks who can prescribe, dispense, or approve medications.
Developer asks how permissions differ by role.
Developer discusses accountability or audit logs for pharmacy actions.

name: Multi-branch operations
description: The system must support multiple pharmacy branches with centralized oversight for pricing, inventory, and operational metrics while keeping local branch-level transactions and stock handling separate.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about multiple branch management.
Developer asks how stock or pricing is centralized or localized per branch.
Developer mentions branch-level reporting or inventory independence.

name: Inventory and expiry tracking
description: The system must track stock levels, batch numbers, expiry dates, manufacturer information, and low-stock warnings so expired or near-expiry items can be managed before they affect care.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about stock levels or reorder thresholds.
Developer discusses expiry dates, batches, or product recall concerns.
Developer mentions stock alerts or preventing medication waste.

name: Prescription workflow and controlled-substance handling
description: The system must handle prescription intake, validation, refill tracking, and restricted medication controls with clear workflows for high-risk or controlled medicines.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks how prescriptions are captured or verified.
Developer inquires about refill rules or repeat prescriptions.
Developer mentions controlled substances or special handling.

name: Payment, billing, and reconciliation
description: The system must support in-store payment flows, insurance or claim settlement processes, and cash reconciliation so the pharmacy can close end-of-day totals accurately and reduce manual errors.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about payment methods or reimbursement.
Developer discusses cash drawers or daily sales reconciliation.
Developer mentions insurance billing or claim support.

name: Reporting and operational dashboards
description: The pharmacy needs reporting for sales, inventory movement, prescription trends, margin analysis, branch performance, and operational KPIs to support management decisions.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about dashboards, KPIs, or reports.
Developer mentions sales trends, stock movement, or branch comparisons.
Developer discusses operational visibility for management.

name: Supplier and purchasing workflow
description: The system must support purchase orders, supplier records, lead times, and reorder planning so essential medications can be procured efficiently while controlling costs.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about supplier records or purchase orders.
Developer mentions reorder triggers or lead times.
Developer discusses procurement and cost control.

name: Customer and patient records
description: The system must maintain basic customer or patient records, relevant prescription history, and note-taking that supports repeat purchases, reminder workflows, and safer service delivery.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about patient records or customer histories.
Developer mentions repeat purchase behavior or reminder messages.
Developer discusses note-taking or record continuity.

name: Operational constraints and integration realities
description: The solution must work in a real-world pharmacy environment, likely with existing accounting or pharmacy software, limited staff training time, and a need for stable, low-friction operations during busy retail hours.
evidenceCriteria: Developer asks about system integration with current tools.
Developer mentions training burden, staff adoption, or downtime risk.
Developer discusses operational constraints such as low internet, fast checkout, or legacy systems.
